title: First Columbia sides, May 1940
summary: Hughes reports the two Columbia sides she doesn't have; Roy Eldridge and Charlie Shavers noted.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: To stick with the chronology of your recordings, we now come to your first pair of sides with Columbia.
And in these two, I have not been able to find so I haven't heard them. But they were recorded on the 1st of May 1940.
"St. Louis Blues" again and "The Hour of Parting."

I don't have those either. But it'll be interesting to note that Roy Eldridge played along with the Kirby Orchestra on this too. I don't know how Roy happened to wonder into the studio. But he was on "Hour of Parting" and "St. Louis Blues" too. It says Charlie Shavers was there, but it was actually Roy Eldridge.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well that's worth noting, certainly, for Roy Eldridge fans.

I wound up having to record 'St. Louis Blues' for several different outfits too. It got to be a pretty big number. In fact, that was one of the numbers in my repertoire that I had to do when I was doing vaudeville -- one of the four selections; 'Loch Lomond,' 'St. Louis Blues', and any two I could find in-between that were currently popular. But those are the standards.
